requirement:
YAML reports only `Comment` attachments. Each `#` comment is one attachment,
including a comment following a mapping value. A `#` within quoted text or
within the content of a block scalar belongs to the scalar.
rationale:
The requirement `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.attachments` has one {test} site, `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]`. Its implementation site is `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/languages/yaml.rs#static[PROFILE]`. I did not read that implementation, because the judgment rests on the test's inputs and assertions.

The test's `test.yaml` case uses the source `a: |\n  # literal\n# standalone\nb: '# literal' # real\nc: "# literal"\n`. It asserts that the collected attachments are exactly `[(Comment, "# standalone"), (Comment, "# real")]`. Each obligation maps to this case as follows:

- **Only `Comment` attachments:** The test compares each attachment's kind and text. Any `Annotation` or other kind would fail the exact-vector comparison.
- **Each `#` comment is one attachment:** The standalone comment on its own line is reported as one attachment.
- **Comment following a mapping value:** `b: '# literal' # real` yields `# real` as a separate attachment.
- **`#` in a block scalar belongs to the scalar:** `# literal` inside `a: |` is not reported.
- **`#` in quoted text belongs to the scalar:** The single-quoted `'# literal'` and the double-quoted `"# literal"` are not reported. The comparison is exact, so any extra attachment would fail.

I found one thing the test doesn't do. It has no case with several consecutive YAML comment lines, which would check that each line is a separate attachment. The TOML case in the same test does cover consecutive comments. The comment-node handling looks shared across the profiles, and the YAML profile identifies comments by node kind. The text doesn't call out this scenario as a distinct boundary, so I don't count it as a gap.

No {fixme} acknowledgments apply. The test is correctly marked with `{test}` for this requirement.
